title: Wrong day, Kenta
setting: A cold late morning in the flat Kenta shares with Sora. Kenta barges into Sora's room to get him up for work at twelve.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: sora, okite! mou juuichiji da yo.
lines.ja: ソラ、起きて！もう十一時だよ。
lines.kana: そら、おきて！もうじゅういちじだよ。
lines.english: Sora, get up! It's already eleven.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.ja: うん、もうちょっとだけ。
lines.kana: うん、もうちょっとだけ。

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.ja: だめ。カーテン開けるよ。
lines.kana: だめ。カーテンあけるよ。

lines.speaker: sora
lines.ja: うわ、まぶしい！カーテン閉めて！
lines.kana: うわ、まぶしい！カーテンしめて！
lines.english: Argh, that's bright! Close the curtains!

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: shimenai yo. mado mo akeru ne.
lines.ja: 閉めないよ。窓も開けるね。
lines.kana: しめないよ。まどもあけるね。
lines.english: Nope, they're staying open. And I'm opening the window too.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: e, nande mado akeru no? samui yo!
lines.ja: え、なんで窓開けるの？寒いよ！
lines.kana: え、なんでまどあけるの？さむいよ！
lines.english: What? Why are you opening the window? It's freezing!

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: datte, kono heya, osake no nioi suru yo. kinou nonda no?
lines.ja: だって、この部屋、お酒の匂いするよ。昨日飲んだの？
lines.kana: だって、このへや、おさけのにおいするよ。きのうのんだの？
lines.english: Because this room smells of booze. Were you drinking last night?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: un, chotto ne. dakara atama itai n da yo.
lines.ja: うん、ちょっとね。だから頭痛いんだよ。
lines.kana: うん、ちょっとね。だからあたまいたいんだよ。
lines.english: Yeah, a little. That's why my head hurts.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: ii kara, okite. kyou, juuniji kara shigoto da yo ne?
lines.ja: いいから、起きて。今日、十二時から仕事だよね？
lines.kana: いいから、おきて。きょう、じゅうにじからしごとだよね？
lines.english: Never mind that, just get up. You've got work at twelve today, right?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: kyou? uun, sore raishuu da yo.
lines.ja: 今日？ううん、それ来週だよ。
lines.kana: きょう？ううん、それらいしゅうだよ。

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e, honto? gomen! jaa, kaaten shimeru ne.
lines.ja: え、ほんと？ごめん！じゃあ、カーテン閉めるね。
lines.kana: え、ほんと？ごめん！じゃあ、カーテンしめるね。
lines.english: Wait, really? Sorry! Okay, I'll close the curtains.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.english: Shut the window too. I'm cold.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: kaaten wa shimeta kedo, mado wa chotto aketoku yo.
lines.ja: カーテンは閉めたけど、窓はちょっと開けとくよ。
lines.kana: カーテンはしめたけど、まどはちょっとあけとくよ。
lines.english: I've closed the curtains, but I'm leaving the window open a bit.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: a, ame futte kita. mado shimete!
lines.ja: あ、雨降ってきた。窓閉めて！
lines.kana: あ、あめふってきた。まどしめて！
lines.english: Oh, it's started raining. Shut the window!

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: hai hai, mado shimeta yo. oyasumi.
lines.ja: はいはい、窓閉めたよ。おやすみ。
lines.kana: はいはい、まどしめたよ。おやすみ。
lines.english: All right, all right, the window's shut. Sleep well.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: aa, mou nerarenai yo. kaaten akete.
lines.ja: ああ、もう寝られないよ。カーテン開けて。
lines.kana: ああ、もうねられないよ。カーテンあけて。
lines.english: Ugh, I'll never get back to sleep now. Open the curtains.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.english: Oh, come on! Open them yourself!

choices.english: Kenta wakes Sora because he's late for work at twelve, and Sora hurries out into the rain.
Kenta wakes Sora for a shift that turns out to be next week; once everything is shut again, Sora can't get back to sleep.
Sora wants the window open because his room smells of alcohol, but Kenta shuts it when it starts to rain.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-6: Kenta gets Sora up by opening the curtains and then the window. Line 9: he thinks Sora has work at twelve today, but in line 10 Sora says that's next week (sore raishuu da yo). Kenta apologises and closes the curtains (lines 11 and 13), and shuts the window once it starts raining (lines 14-15). Line 16: by now Sora is wide awake (mou nerarenai) and wants the curtains open again, and in line 17 Kenta tells him to do it himself. A is wrong: there is no work today, and nobody goes out. C is wrong: it's Kenta who opens the window because of the smell (lines 5-7); Sora wants it shut because he's cold (lines 6 and 12).

questions.english: You're round at Kenta's. He walks in from the kitchen and says, "uwa, kono heya atsui ne." (Whew, it's hot in this room.) Offer to open the window.
questions.kana: うわ、このへやあついね。
questions.answer: Offer with mado and akeru, as a question: mado akete ii? (mind if I open the window?) or mado akeyou ka? (shall I open the window?).

modelAnswers.english: Yeah. Mind if I open the window?
It really is. Shall I open the window?

questions.explanation: Someone opening a window uses akeru, the verb Kenta uses in line 5 (mado mo akeru ne) and Sora throws back at him in line 6 (nande mado akeru no?). As an offer it's usually a question: akete ii? asks if it's okay, akeyou ka? offers to do it. Don't say mado aiteru here: that describes a window that is already open, not you opening it.

questions.english: Sora is shivering on the sofa and says, "samui! mado aiteru yo!" (It's freezing! The window's open!) You opened it earlier. Say sorry and that you'll shut it.
questions.kana: さむい！まどあいてるよ！
questions.answer: Apologise and say you'll close it, with mado and shimeru: gomen, mado shimeru ne.

modelAnswers.romaji: a, gomen. ima mado shimeru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: あ、ごめん。今窓閉めるよ。
modelAnswers.english: Oh, sorry. I'll close the window right now.

questions.explanation: Sora's aiteru describes the window's state: it's open. What you do about it is shimeru, someone shutting it, as Sora asks in lines 12 and 14 (mado mo shimete, mado shimete!) and Kenta reports in line 15 (mado shimeta yo). Not mado shimaru: shimaru is the window itself closing (mado shimatteru, the window is shut), not someone shutting it.

questions.english: When Kenta lets the daylight in, what does Sora shout?
questions.ja: ソラさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: そらさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: sora-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Argh, that's bright! Draw the curtains! (hiku, pull)
Argh, that's bright! Open the curtains!
Argh, that's bright! Close the curtains!

questions.explanation: Line 4: Kenta has just opened the curtains (line 3: kaaten akeru yo) and the light hurts (mabushii), so Sora wants them shut: kaaten shimete. A is English 'draw the curtains' put into Japanese word for word (hiku, pull). Japanese does have kaaten o hiku, but it's mostly written and, like 'draw', it doesn't say which way, so in speech people name the direction with shimeru or akeru. B, kaaten akete, is the opposite direction: that's what Kenta has just done, and Sora only asks for it at the very end, once he's given up on sleep (line 16). Kenta closes them with the same verb in lines 11 and 13 (kaaten shimeru ne, kaaten wa shimeta kedo).

newWords.english: dazzling, too bright (light in your eyes)
